connector: Three chapters of the Dwarf’s story are done. Caspian started in a castle full of Telmarines. He ends the week in a moonlit glade full of Fauns. Today, line up every group you met, say what each one wants, and find the two groups that are heading straight for each other.

a.raw: the telmarines had swords but the old narnians had something stronger the memory of aslan so they refused to give up
a.fixed: The Telmarines had swords, but the Old Narnians had something stronger — the memory of Aslan, so they refused to give up.
a.why: Capitals on Telmarines, Old Narnians and Aslan; a comma before but and before so; a dash sets off the important detail; a period ends it.

b.raw: nikabrik hated the telmarines so he did not trust caspian at first
b.fixed: Nikabrik hated the Telmarines, so he did not trust Caspian at first.
b.why: Capitals on the names; a comma before so joins the cause to its result; a period ends it.

vocab: A private teacher who teaches one student or a few.
Someone who takes power, like a throne, without the right to it.
The study of the stars, planets and sky.
In a strict, serious, firm way.
notes.wordParts: Latin bases: port = carry, tract = pull or draw, struct = build: transport, attract, construct, instructed.
notes.grammar: But and so join two complete sentences. But says the second part goes against what you expected; so says the second part happens because of the first. Put a comma before each. Editing day: check that each but or so carries the right logic.
notes.spelling: Suffix rules: drop the silent e (hope + ing = hoping); change y to i (empty + er = emptier); double the last consonant when the last syllable is stressed (begin + ing = beginning, but visit + ing = visiting).

transcripts.welcome: Hello, it’s Nell. Three chapters of the Dwarf’s story are done. A castle, a storm, a cave, a forge, a moonlit dance. Today’s question: what changed for Caspian this week, and what made the change possible?
transcripts.read: Line up every group you met this week, from Miraz’s court to the Fauns. Say what each group wants. Then find the two groups that want opposite things. They’re going to meet, and when they do, it won’t be gentle.
transcripts.grammar: Editing day. Read each sentence with but or so, and ask if the logic is right. They were outnumbered, but they fought anyway. That works. They were outnumbered, so they fought anyway. That doesn’t. One small word, and the meaning flips.
